# Kinetic Studio

> Local, programmatic motion-graphics video engine: a short JSON spec (scenes on a beat grid plus timeline markers) becomes a finished, beat-synced MP4 with procedural music and sound effects, mixed to -14 LUFS and automatically audited. Five modes: kinetic type, explainer, product promo, data story, social quote or karaoke. Runs on the CPU with Python, Skia and ffmpeg; no API key, no account, no cloud call. MIT licence.

Agents use it through an MCP server (stdio or streamable HTTP), function-calling schemas, a one-shot JSON command line or plain Python. The server needs no extra dependencies:

- MCP command: `uvx --from git+https://github.com/28naem-del/kinetic-studio kstudio-mcp` (from a clone: `python -m kstudio.mcp_server`; HTTP: add `--http 8765`, endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`)
- Tools: `list_modes`, `list_scenes`, `get_schema`, `validate_spec`, `new_spec`, `preview`, `render` (progress notifications), `audit`. Each returns one JSON object with an `ok` field; failures carry `error: {code, message, hint}`.
- Workflow: get_schema(mode) -> write the spec from the example -> validate_spec and fix every error -> preview and look at the contact sheet -> render -> report output path and audit verdict.
- Write every scene length in beats (`"4b"`, `"1/2b"`, `"1bar"`); times can name markers (`"drop-2b"`).

metadata:
  version: "0.2"

# Kinetic Studio

A local, programmatic video engine. You write a small JSON spec (scenes on a beat grid plus timeline
markers); the engine renders it in parallel with motion blur and a film grade, scores it with
procedural music and sound effects locked to the beat, mixes to -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP and audits the
file. Same spec, same video: renders are deterministic and resumable.

## When to use

- Short vertical or landscape videos built from words, numbers, charts, UI mock-ups and logos:
  teasers, announcements, explainers, product promos, KPI or market recaps, quotes, captions.
- Anything that should cut on the beat of the music.

Not for: generating live-action footage, faces or voices, lip-sync or text-to-speech. A user's own
photo can go in an `image` scene and their own video in a `clip` scene (any mode: trimmed on the
beat, with titles, captions or counters drawn over it in `over`). The engine does not write copy:
you write the words from the brief.

## 30-second path

Pick one way in. All three run the same engine and return the same JSON.

**MCP (any MCP-capable agent).** Register the server, then call its tools:

```
command: uvx
args:    ["--from", "git+https://github.com/28naem-del/kinetic-studio", "kstudio-mcp"]
```

From a clone instead: `python -m kstudio.mcp_server` with the clone as working directory.
Per-framework snippets: `docs/quickstarts/`.

**Command line.**

```
kstudio new kinetic my-reel            # starter project from the mode's example
kstudio validate my-reel               # errors with JSON Pointer paths and hints
kstudio preview my-reel                # stills + contact_sheet.jpg in a few seconds
kstudio render my-reel                 # my-reel/out/my-reel_reel.mp4 + .report.json
```

`kstudio --json <command>` prints exactly one JSON object; exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage, 3 spec
invalid, 4 render failed, 5 audit failed, 6 missing tool (`kstudio doctor` checks ffmpeg and the
rest). `kinetic-studio` is the same command.

**Function calling without MCP.** Load `docs/tools/functions.json` (or `tools.schema.json`) as
your tool list and dispatch each call with
`from kstudio.mcp_server import run_tool; run_tool(name, arguments_json)`.

## Workflow (brief -> video)

| step | MCP tool | command line |
|---|---|---|
| 1. see what exists | `list_modes`, `list_scenes` | `kstudio modes`, `kstudio scenes -v` |
| 2. get the contract | `get_schema {mode}` (schema + example spec) | `kstudio schema --mode <m>`, `docs/SCENES.md` |
| 3. start a project | `new_spec {mode, dir, spec_json?}` | `kstudio new <mode> <dir>` |
| 4. check the spec | `validate_spec {spec_path}` | `kstudio validate <dir>` |
| 5. look before rendering | `preview {spec_path}` (contact sheet image) | `kstudio preview <dir>` |
| 6. render | `render {spec_path}` (progress notifications) | `kstudio render <dir>` |
| 7. verify | `audit {video, mode}` (render already audits) | `kstudio audit <video> --mode <m>` |

1. **Pick the mode** from the brief (table below). If unclear, default to `kinetic`.
2. **Write the spec** from the mode's example: keep its structure, replace the words, numbers and
   colours. 8-15 s for social, one idea per scene.
3. **Validate** and fix every error (each has a JSON Pointer `path`, a `message` and a `hint`).
   Fix warnings about off-grid lengths too.
4. **Preview and look at the contact sheet**: text fits, nothing overlaps, the last frame is the
   intended end card.
5. **Render**, then report the output path, duration, audit verdict and any failed check. If motion
   or hold checks fail, shorten holds, add a scene or use a busier transition; do not relax thresholds.

Interrupted renders resume: run the same render again and finished 2-second chunks are reused
(`fresh: true` / `--fresh` forces a clean render).

## Beat units (the one rule that matters)

Every time and length can be written in beats at the music tempo, and should be:

| write | means |
|---|---|
| `"4b"`, `"1/2b"`, `"3/4b"` | 4 beats, half a beat, three quarters of a beat |
| `"1bar"`, `"2bars"` | one bar (4 beats), two bars |
| `"bar3"` | the start of bar 3 (1-based, like a DAW) |
| `"drop"`, `"drop-2b"`, `"intro+1.25s"`, `"end-1b"` | a named marker or scene id, with offsets |
| `1.5`, `"1.5s"`, `"250ms"` | seconds (avoid for scene lengths) |

- Scene lengths: whole beats, ideally 2b, 4b or 8b. Cuts, transition windows and their sound
  effects then land on the grid. Validation warns when a length is off the grid.
- `"snap": true` in the spec (or `snap` on render) moves seconds-valued lengths and starts onto the
  beat grid.
- With your own music (`"music": {"file": "track.mp3"}`) the tempo and downbeat come from the file.

## JSON contract

**Spec** (comments and trailing commas allowed; full schema: `get_schema`):

```jsonc
{
  "mode": "kinetic",                       // kinetic | explainer | promo | data | social
  "handle": "@you",                        // small corner handle (optional)
  "theme": "ink",                          // ink | lab | studio | terminal | warm, or {"base": "ink", "accent": "#ff3b30"}
  "music": { "style": "drive", "bpm": 128 },  // drive | calm | bright | pulse | lofi | none, or {"file": "track.mp3"}
  "transition": "whip",                    // default between scenes
  "markers": [
    { "kind": "section", "at": 0, "name": "intro", "energy": 1 },   // energy 0-3 drives music layers and camera
    { "kind": "section", "at": "drop", "name": "drop", "energy": 3 },
    { "kind": "sfx", "at": "drop-2b", "sound": "riser_short" },
    { "kind": "hit", "at": "8b", "strength": 0.8 },
    { "kind": "lower_third", "at": "1b", "dur": "4b", "tag": "Note", "text": "..." }
  ],
  "scenes": [
    { "type": "slam", "id": "open", "words": ["STOP", "SCROLLING"], "dur": "4b" },
    { "type": "stack", "lines": ["ONE IDEA", "PER", "BEAT"], "dur": "4b", "transition": "whip-left" },
    { "type": "burst", "id": "drop", "text": "GO", "dur": "4b", "transition": "flash" }
  ]
}
```

Transitions (per scene, on the incoming one): `cut`, `flash`, `cross` (alias `fade`), `dissolve`,
`whip`, `push`, `zoom`, `squash`, `wipe` (`rect`, `circle`, `diagonal`, `type`), `slice`, `split`,
`match` (shared-element hand-off). Shorthand `"whip-left"`, `"wipe-circle"`, or a dict
`{"kind": "wipe", "shape": "circle", "dur": "1b", "dir": "up", "on": "downbeat"}`.

**Tool results.** Every tool returns one JSON object. `ok` says whether the thing asked about is good
(spec valid, video rendered and audited). On failure there is `error: {code, message, hint}` and the
MCP result has `isError: true`; validation problems are a normal result with `ok: false` and an
`errors` list. Codes: `USAGE`, `MODE_UNKNOWN`, `DIR_NOT_EMPTY`, `FILE_NOT_FOUND`, `SPEC_INVALID`,
`SPEC_NOT_FOUND`, `SPEC_PARSE`, `RENDER_FAILED`, `MISSING_TOOL`, `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## Modes

| mode | use for | look / sound | example scenes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kinetic` | hype teasers, announcements, hooks | ink: black, bone, signal red; whips; `drive` 128 BPM | `slam`, `stack`, `marquee`, `type3d`, `scramble`, `countdown`, `burst` |
| `explainer` | education, "what is X" | lab: editorial paper, navy, cobalt; crosses; `calm` 84 BPM | `cover`, `definition`, `diagram`, `bullets`, `keyfact`, `end_card` |
| `promo` | app and product launches | studio: violet gradient; pushes; `bright` 112 BPM | `device`, `features`, `cta`, `brand`, `logo`, `image` |
| `data` | market, crypto, KPI stories | terminal: green up, red down; cuts; `pulse` 120 BPM | `counter`, `line`, `candles`, `bars`, `stat_grid`, `ticker` |
| `social` | quotes, tips, spoken-line captions | warm: espresso, amber; `lofi` 86 BPM | `hook`, `quote`, `karaoke`, `follow`, `text` |

Any scene works in any mode; the mode only sets theme, music, camera feel, default transition and
audit thresholds. Parameters per scene: `list_scenes {type}` or `docs/SCENES.md`.

## Brief -> spec rules per mode

**kinetic.** Hook in the first 2 beats (`slam`, 2-4 words). One idea per scene, 2-4 words per line;
capitals read best. Build energy with sections 1 -> 2 -> 3, put `riser_short` 2 beats before the
drop, end on `burst` or `logo`.

**explainer.** `cover` (the question) -> `definition` -> `diagram` or `keyfact` -> `bullets` ->
`end_card`. 4-8 beats per scene, at most ~6 words per bullet. Put citations in `sources` (author,
journal, year) timed to the scene they support. For health or medical topics:
- describe what it is and where it is "studied in" / "researched for"; never say it treats, cures,
  prevents, reverses or is safe or effective;
- no doses, routes, protocols, sourcing or before/after claims;
- end on `end_card` with "For learning only." / "Not medical advice." (the defaults).

For finance, add "Illustrative data - not financial advice" in a `lower_third`.

**promo.** `device` hero (headline = product name, 2-3 callouts, `screen: "shot.png"` for a real
screenshot in the project directory, else a procedural UI) -> `features` (4 items, 2-3 word title
plus a short line) -> `cta` (verb-first button) -> `brand` or `logo` (wordmark, tagline, url).

**data.** Lead with the single most striking number (`counter`), then 2-3 charts, end on `ticker` or
`stat_grid`. Use real numbers from the brief; if they are illustrative, say so in a `lower_third`.
`line` takes `series` (numbers) or a seeded random walk `{"seed", "n", "start", "drift", "vol"}`;
`candles` takes `ohlc` (`[o, h, l, c]` rows) or the same keys.

**social.** `hook` -> `quote` (at most 20 words, author and role) and/or `karaoke` with the spoken
line (`"timing": "beat"`, or per-word `"words": [{"w": "Make", "t": 0.0}, ...]` from a transcript,
2-3 `emphasis` words) -> `follow`.

## Output options

Presets: `reel` / `story` 1080x1920, `landscape` / `youtube` 1920x1080, `square` 1080x1080,
`portrait` 1080x1350; `k4` / `--4k` doubles both sides. Frame rates 24, 25, 30, 50, 60. Quality
`draft` (no motion blur, for checks), `standard` (default), `high`.

## Troubleshooting

| symptom | fix |
|---|---|
| `MISSING_TOOL` / ffmpeg not found | install ffmpeg with libx264 (`brew install ffmpeg`, `apt install ffmpeg`) |
| `SPEC_PARSE` | the spec must be one JSON object; check quotes and brackets |
| `SPEC_INVALID` with a `path` | fix that field; the `hint` names the allowed values |
| warning "not a whole number of beats" | write the length as `"4b"` or set `"snap": true` |
| text clipped or overlapping in the contact sheet | shorter words, fewer lines, or a smaller `size` / `weight` |
| audit fails `motion_ratio` or `longest_hold` | shorter scenes, a busier transition, an extra scene |
| audit fails `loudness` / `true_peak` | re-render; with your own track, lower `music.gain` |
| render slow or memory-bound | `quality: "draft"` while iterating; fewer `workers` |
| MCP client times out on `render` | raise its tool timeout to 15 minutes (a 15 s reel renders in a few minutes) or use `preview` first |
| render interrupted | run it again: finished chunks resume |

## Limits

- A 15-second 1080x1920 / 30 fps reel at `standard` takes about 1-3 minutes on a 10-core laptop
  (4-13x the video length; more on a busy machine). `draft` is faster; use `preview` while iterating.
- Pure 2D/2.5D motion graphics: no footage generation, no lip-sync, no voice-over. Footage you
  supply plays in a `clip` scene.
- Optional character swap: `kstudio swap` / the MCP tool `swap` / a clip's `source.swap` send a video
  and a character image to a ComfyUI server you run on an NVIDIA GPU with Openjutsu's workflows
  (`KSTUDIO_COMFY_URL`). Without one they return `BACKEND_UNREACHABLE` (exit 7) and a clip plays the
  input video. Nothing else needs it. See `docs/SWAP.md`.
- Do not post or upload results anywhere without the user's explicit approval.

<!-- docs/tools/README.md -->

# Tool definitions

Kinetic Studio's eight tools, described once in `kstudio/mcp_server.py` (`TOOLS`) and exported here
for clients that do not speak MCP. Do not edit the JSON files by hand.

| file | for |
|---|---|
| `mcp-tools.json` | the MCP `tools/list` result, exactly as the server returns it |
| `functions.json` | function tools in the flat form `{"type": "function", "name", "description", "parameters", "strict": true}` |
| `functions-chat.json` | the same tools in the nested form `{"type": "function", "function": {...}}` used by chat-completions style APIs |
| `tools.schema.json` | a plain manifest: name, description, input and output JSON Schema, hints and the ways to invoke the server |
| `generate.py` | writes the four files from `TOOLS` and `/llms-full.txt` from the docs; `--check` fails when any is out of date; `--scenes` rewrites `docs/SCENES.md` from the scene registry |

```bash
python docs/tools/generate.py           # regenerate after changing a tool or the skill and docs
python docs/tools/generate.py --check   # what the test suite runs (tests/test_mcp.py)
```

## Names and arguments

Function-calling exports name each tool `kstudio_<tool>` (for example `kstudio_render`) so they do
not collide with other tools; MCP uses the bare names. The dispatcher accepts both.

The function schemas are in strict form: every property is listed as required and the optional ones
accept `null`. The server treats `null` as "not given", so a model can fill every field.

## Dispatching calls

```python
import json
from kstudio.mcp_server import run_tool

tools = json.load(open("docs/tools/functions.json"))   # pass to your model API as its tool list

def on_tool_call(name: str, arguments: str) -> str:
    """name: "kstudio_validate_spec" or "validate_spec"; arguments: the JSON text from the model."""
    return json.dumps(run_tool(name, arguments))           # one JSON object with an "ok" field
```

From a shell or another language: `python -m kstudio.mcp_server --call <tool> '<json>'` prints the
same JSON object on stdout and exits 0 when `ok` is true.

## The tools

| tool | does | writes files |
|---|---|---|
| `list_modes` | modes with theme, music, transition, example scenes; presets, quality, frame rates, time units | no |
| `list_scenes` | the scene types, or one type's parameters | no |
| `get_schema` | the spec JSON Schema (optionally only some scene types), mode defaults and the mode's example spec | no |
| `validate_spec` | checks a spec file or inline JSON; errors carry a JSON Pointer path, message and hint | no |
| `new_spec` | starts a project directory from a mode's example, or from your spec JSON | yes |
| `preview` | renders stills and a contact sheet (returned as an image) in seconds | yes |
| `render` | renders, mixes and audits the MP4, with progress notifications | yes |
| `audit` | re-checks any MP4 (motion, holds, loudness, true peak, frame count) | yes (report) |

# Quickstarts

Kinetic Studio is a local MCP server, a JSON command line and a set of function-calling schemas, so
it plugs into any agent. Every quickstart below was checked against that framework's current
documentation on 2026-10-30; each page cites the URL it was checked against.

The one line every MCP client needs:

```
uvx --from git+https://github.com/28naem-del/kinetic-studio kstudio-mcp
```

(from a clone: `python -m kstudio.mcp_server` with the clone on `PYTHONPATH`; HTTP instead of stdio:
add `--http 8765` and connect to `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`).

## Frameworks (alphabetical)

- [AutoGen and Microsoft Agent Framework](autogen.md): Python, stdio
- [Claude Code](claude-code.md): CLI, stdio
- [Cline](cline.md): editor extension, stdio
- [Codex CLI](codex-cli.md): CLI, stdio
- [Continue](continue.md): editor extension, stdio
- [CrewAI (crew-style multi-agent)](crewai.md): Python, stdio
- [Cursor](cursor.md): editor, stdio
- [Dify](dify.md): platform, HTTP
- [Gemini CLI](gemini-cli.md): CLI, stdio
- [LangChain and LangGraph](langchain.md): Python, stdio
- [n8n](n8n.md): workflow automation, HTTP or Execute Command
- [OpenHands](openhands.md): CLI and web app, stdio or HTTP
- [Plain Python](python.md): no framework: in-process, function calling or raw MCP
- [Plain shell and curl](shell.md): one-shot JSON, raw stdio, curl over HTTP
- [Windsurf](windsurf.md): editor, stdio

## What every client gets

Eight tools: `list_modes`, `list_scenes`, `get_schema`, `validate_spec`, `new_spec`, `preview`,
`render` (with progress notifications) and `audit`. Each takes a JSON Schema-described object and
returns one JSON object with an `ok` field. Definitions for clients without MCP live in `docs/tools/`.

Both MCP protocol eras are served: the stateless 2026-07-28 revision (`server/discover`) and the
`initialize` handshake of 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05.

## The skill

`skills/kinetic-studio/SKILL.md` is a portable skill (frontmatter plus instructions): the workflow,
beat-unit rules, the spec contract and per-mode writing rules. Copy the `skills/kinetic-studio/`
folder into whatever skills directory your agent reads (for example `.agents/skills/`), or paste the
file into the system prompt of agents without skill support.

## Timeouts

A 15-second 1080x1920 reel takes about 1-3 minutes at standard quality on a 10-core laptop (more
on a busy machine); the first start through uvx downloads
the engine. Raise the client's startup and tool timeouts where the quickstart says so, and use
`preview` (seconds) while iterating.

<!-- docs/SCENES.md -->

# Scene reference

32 scene types. Any scene works in any mode; the mode only sets theme, music, camera feel,
default transition and audit thresholds. The same information is live from the `list_scenes` MCP tool
and `kstudio scenes -v`; the full JSON Schema comes from `get_schema`. Regenerate this page with
`python docs/tools/generate.py --scenes`.

## Times and lengths

Every time or length takes seconds (`1.5`, `"1.5s"`, `"250ms"`) or beats at the music tempo:
`"4b"`, `"1/2b"`, `"1bar"`, `"bar3"` (start of bar 3), or a marker or scene id with an offset
(`"drop-2b"`, `"intro+1.25s"`, `"end-1b"`). Write scene lengths in whole beats.

## Keys every scene accepts

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | the scene type (below) |
| `id` | a name other times can refer to (`"drop"`, `"drop-2b"`) |
| `dur` | length, ideally whole beats (`"4b"`) |
| `at` | start time; default: right after the previous scene |
| `transition` | transition into this scene (see below); default: the mode's |
| `transition_dur` | transition window length (`"1/2b"`) |
| `transition_sfx` | `false` silences the transition sound (pick another with `"sfx"` in a transition dict) |
| `ground` | backdrop colour: a theme colour name (default `bg`) or a hex colour |
| `ground_style` | `solid`, `gradient`, `grid`, `dots`, `blobs`, `paper`, `mesh` |
| `camera` | overrides of the mode camera: `push`, `carry`, `drift`, `drift_hz`, `energy`, `roll`, `truck`, `yaw`, `pitch`, `ground_depth`, `bump`, `shake`, `dist` |

## Transitions

Set on the incoming scene: a name, a shorthand (`"whip-left"`, `"wipe-circle"`) or a dict such as
`{"kind": "wipe", "shape": "circle", "dur": "1b", "dir": "up"}`. Directions: `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`. Wipe shapes: `rect`, `circle`, `diagonal`, `type`.

| kind | window (beats) | sound at the cut |
|---|---|---|
| `cut` | 0 | - |
| `flash` | 0 | hit |
| `cross` | 1 | - |
| `fade` (alias of `cross`) | 1 | - |
| `dissolve` | 1 | - |
| `whip` | 0.5 | whoosh |
| `push` | 0.75 | swish |
| `zoom` | 0.75 | whoosh |
| `squash` | 0.5 | swish |
| `wipe` | 1 | swish |
| `slice` | 1 | swish |
| `split` | 0.75 | swish |
| `match` | 0 | - |

## Explainer

### `bullets`

Numbered list with large display numerals (headline 168): the heading (title 126) on the anchor and the list's rules and ghosted numerals on beat 0, then one item per `stagger` (default 1b) from `first` (default 1b) with a tick: its numeral and accent rule come in, its text rises, and the previous item steps back to muted. Rows share the anchor -> bottom safe line. Items are strings or {text, detail, icon}; numbered false sets check marks.

Beats 2, 3, ...: one figure of `stats` per beat on the bottom safe line; numeric figures after the first count up from the first one (a slow miss reads slow).

Call to action on the grid: tracked `kicker`, the `headline` (168 px, 700) flush-left on the shared anchor, a full-width pill button that springs in on beat 1 and pulses on every beat (spring landing one frame after the kick, with a ring wave), a touch that presses it on the downbeat `tap_at` (click SFX + ripple; the label morphs to `done` if set), a `note` under the button and the `sub` line (platforms) on the bottom safe line. `lockup` (product name) puts a small app icon (`mark`) + name on the top safe line so the block spans the frame.

### `device`

Hero device shot. A phone at `height` of the frame (0.70) springs up from below and turns in yaw from yaw[0] to yaw[1] (in_out_quint over `tilt`, default 4b), then eases back half way over the rest of the shot; the bezel highlight and glass sheen follow the tilt; a soft contact + ambient shadow sits under it. Above it: an optional tracked `kicker`, the `headline` at the headline role (168 px, 700) flush-left on the grid, and `sub` set as a right-aligned standfirst. `callouts` ({text, icon, side, y, x, dy, color}) pop in on the beat (`first_callout`, `callout_gap`): a pill (spring) inside the safe area with a leader line to the point (x, y) on the screen (fractions of the screen), tracked through the tilt. `screen` = screenshot path (9:19.5) or the procedural `ui`; `scroll` = list scroll (px@1080). Legacy `swing` (degrees) sets a symmetric yaw when `yaw` is not given.

| key | default |
|---|---|
| `frame` | `"phone"` |
| `screen` | `""` |
| `ui` | `{}` |
| `kicker` | `""` |
| `headline` | `""` |

| `scroll` | `0` |

| `land` | `"1b"` |

Items: {icon, title, text, color}. `layout: "grid"` (or `columns` > 0) keeps the v0.1 cards.

## Any mode

### `end_card`

Closing card on the grid, flush-left from the shared top anchor: a brand lockup (accent badge with an icon + wordmark on the subhead role), the statement (title role), an accent line (body), a CTA pill and the one handle, with small print standing on the bottom safe line. Elements enter one per half beat on the registry "enter" ease and the badge and CTA arrow pulse on every beat. The card owns the handle: the film's corner handle is hidden while it is on screen, and the handle colour is picked for >= 4.5:1 contrast on the card's ground.

| key | default |
|---|---|
| `icon` | `"book"` |

## Footage (any mode)

### `clip`

Footage from a local video file: trim with `in`/`out` (seconds or beats, snapped with the grid), `fit` cover (with a `focus` point and a slow `zoom`) or contain, an optional `grade`, `blur` and `opacity`, a `scrim` that keeps type legible, an optional picture-in-picture `box`, and `over`: a list of scenes (title, callout, karaoke, counter ...) drawn on top of the footage. `end` = hold (freeze the last frame) or loop. `source` = {"swap": {...}} plays footage from the optional swap backend (see docs/SWAP.md) and falls back to the input video without it.

| key | default |
|---|---|
| `src` | `""` |
| `source` | `null` |
| `in` | `0.0` |
| `out` | `null` |
| `speed` | `1.0` |
| `end` | `"hold"` |
| `fit` | `"cover"` |
| `focus` | `[0.5, 0.5]` |
| `zoom` | `[1.0, 1.06]` |
| `ease` | `"move"` |
| `opacity` | `1.0` |
| `grade` | `null` |
| `blur` | `0.0` |
| `scrim` | `0.45` |
| `box` | `null` |
| `radius` | `24` |
| `backdrop` | `"blur"` |
| `sfx` | `null` |
| `over` | `[]` |

---

<!-- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md -->

# Architecture

```
            agents (MCP stdio / streamable HTTP)   function calling   shell
                       │                                  │              │
                       ▼                                  ▼              ▼
            mcp_server.py: 8 tools ─────── run_tool() ──────── --call / cli.py (kstudio)
                       │
spec.json ──► spec.py (JSONC / JS loader, hash) ──► schema.py (JSON Schema from the engine, validation, fix hints)
                       │
                       ▼
                  film.py  Film
                       │  timeline.py: markers, beat grid, time expressions ("4b", "bar3", "drop-2b")
                       │  scenes/*: 31 types, each = draw(ctx) + cues() + shutter()
                       │  transitions.py: beat-quantised windows (cut ... match), element hand-off
                       │  camera.py: 2.5D dolly, parallax, drift with continuity across cuts
                       │  layout.py: 12-column grid, safe zones, type scale
                       ▼
pipeline.build ─► render.py ── N spawn workers (resources.py: free RAM / CPU)
                 │              each: compositor.py → Skia raster → linear-light motion blur
                 │              → grade.py (tone curve, split toning) → bloom / vignette / grain
                 │              → libx264 chunk, verified with ffprobe, renamed atomically (resume)
                 │            concat (-c copy, +faststart)
                 ├─► audio/mix.py: bed (audio/music.py procedural styles | user file | none)
                 │              + SFX (audio/synth.py kit) from sfx markers and transition cues,
                 │              ducking, loudness → gain → true-peak limiter, iterate to -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP
                 ├─► mux (AAC 48 kHz)
                 └─► audit.py: ffprobe + decoded motion analysis + loudness → PASS/FAIL report.json
```

Renders are deterministic: a frame is a pure function of (spec, time), so any worker can draw any
frame and an interrupted render resumes from its finished 2-second chunks.

## Interfaces

| module | role |
|---|---|
| `mcp_server.py` | zero-dependency MCP server: stdio (default) and streamable HTTP (`--http`); both protocol eras (2026-07-28 stateless with `server/discover`, and `initialize` for 2025-11-25 / 2025-06-18 / 2025-03-26 / 2024-11-05); tools `list_modes`, `list_scenes`, `get_schema`, `validate_spec`, `new_spec`, `preview`, `render` (progress notifications, cancellable), `audit`; `run_tool()` for in-process function calling; `--call` for one-shot JSON |
| `cli.py` | the `kstudio` command (`modes`, `scenes`, `new`, `info`, `preview`, `render`, `audit`, `mix`, `beats`, `sfx`) |
| `schema.py` | the spec JSON Schema built at run time from the scene registry and engine tables; validator with JSON Pointer paths, hints and a repair prompt |
| `exitcodes.py` | exit codes and machine-readable error codes shared by the command line and the tools |
| `brief.py` | brief → prompt pack (system prompt, schema, examples, beat rules) for any model; no model call |
| `docs/tools/generate.py` | exports the MCP tool list as function-calling schemas and a manifest; `--check` keeps them in sync |

## Engine

| module | role |
|---|---|
| `spec.py` | loads JSON with comments and trailing commas (or a JS module's default export) |
| `timeline.py` | `Timeline` / `Marker`: sections with energy 0-3, cues, captions, sfx, hits; seconds, beats, bars and named-marker expressions; beat ↔ time on the grid |
| `beats.py` | onset envelope + autocorrelation tempo + phase fit → `BeatGrid` from any audio file |
| `film.py` | builds scenes on the timeline, resolves markers and snapping, emits scene cues and transition sounds, draws the frame at time t |
| `scenes/` | `kinetic`, `explainer`, `promo`, `data`, `social` and `common` scene families on a shared `base.Scene` (grounds: solid, gradient, grid, dots, blobs, paper, mesh) |
| `transitions.py` | 13 transition kinds with beat-length windows, anchors, shutter multipliers and default sounds; wipe shapes, directions, shared-element `match` |
| `camera.py` | per-mode and per-scene camera (push, carry, drift, roll, truck, yaw, pitch, bump, shake ...) |
| `layout.py` | grid and type roles at 1080 reference px, scaled to any preset |
| `ease.py` | easing grammar, springs with bounded overshoot, staggers, deterministic noise |
| `draw.py`, `fonts.py` | Skia helpers, icons, palettes, variable-font instancing |
| `compositor.py` | adaptive sub-frame motion blur, post chain, dithered output |
| `grade.py` | colour grades `neutral`, `ink`, `lab`, `studio`, `terminal`, `warm` compiled to lookup tables |
| `modes.py` | 5 themes and per-mode music, camera, post, transition and audit defaults |
| `presets.py` | output presets (reel, story, landscape, youtube, square, portrait) and quality levels (draft, standard, high) |
| `render.py`, `pipeline.py` | chunk planning, worker pool, encoder, manifest and resume, concat, mix, mux, audit, report |
| `resources.py` | free-RAM and CPU aware worker count |
| `preview.py` | stills at scene middles and transitions plus a contact sheet |
| `audit.py` | codec, frame rate, frames, duration, motion ratio, longest hold, black frames, loudness, true peak, A/V gap, with per-mode thresholds |

## Audio

| module | role |
|---|---|
| `audio/music.py` | 5 arranged styles (`drive`, `calm`, `bright`, `pulse`, `lofi`) following section energy: fills, risers, sidechain, hard stop |
| `audio/instruments.py` | synthesised drums, bass, keys and pads (no samples) |
| `audio/synth.py` | 29 synthesised sound effects (14 of them UI sounds) with peak offsets for alignment |
| `audio/mix.py` | bed + effects, ducking, LUFS normalisation, look-ahead limiter |
| `audio/dsp.py` | NumPy DSP: envelopes, filters, oscillators, convolution reverb, WAV I/O |
